Her work focused on the mathematical framework of non-Abelian gauge theories, which underpin QCD as the theory of the strong nuclear force. Marchetti's research provided key insights into asymptotic freedom, a property discovered by David Gross, Frank Wilczek, and David Politzer, for which they later received the Nobel Prize. She also contributed to early lattice gauge theory simulations, helping to model how quarks are confined within protons and neutrons, preventing their isolation. Her papers from this period remain influential in understanding the behavior of strong interactions at high energies.
